instruction: Using VLC, rotate the upside-down video file on the Desktop by 180 degrees and save the corrected version as 'AppleMacintosh1984.mp4' to the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires agent to rotate the upside-down video 180 degrees in VLC and save it with the new filename 'AppleMacintosh1984.mp4' on Desktop. Evaluator verifies: (1) output file exists at expected location, (2) video has rotation=0 (meaning it was properly corrected from the flipped original), and (3) file size is reasonable (>100KB) to ensure it's not corrupted or just a renamed copy. Uses ffprobe to extract video metadata for rotation verification.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator checks all requirements - file existence at correct path, video rotation metadata (rotation=0 for upright video), and file integrity (min_size > 100KB)
Correct transformation verification: Getter extracts video rotation metadata using ffprobe (industry-standard tool), checking both side_data_list and tags for rotation values
Prevents false positives: The rotation check ensures agent cannot simply rename/copy the original flipped video - the output must have rotation=0 (upright) while input has rotation=180
Robust logic: Metric normalizes rotation values (mod 360), handles edge cases (missing metadata with partial credit 0.7), and verifies file size to prevent corrupted outputs
Semantically correct expected values: rotation=0 is correct for a properly upright video (no rotation metadata needed), min_size=100000 ensures file is not corrupted or empty
